claims.text: Incorporating a second platinum-group metal into a monometallic PGM nanoscale catalyst alters its surface electronic structure.
Changes in surface electronic structure modulate the adsorption energies of ethanol and its intermediates.
Changes in surface electronic structure modulate the activation energies associated with ethanol oxidation.
Electronic effects induced by PGM alloying enhance ethanol-oxidation activity and selectivity.
The relevant electronic mediators include the catalyst's d-band-center position and surface charge density.
Alloying changes the adsorption energies of ethanol and critical oxidation intermediates.
Alloying changes activation barriers for ethanol and critical oxidation intermediates.
The alloy-induced energetic changes favor more complete ethanol oxidation toward carbon dioxide.
The alloy-induced energetic changes reduce catalyst-surface poisoning.
Reduced poisoning and altered reaction energetics increase the ethanol-oxidation rate.
Reduced poisoning and altered reaction energetics improve product selectivity.
Alloyed catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density than unmodified monometallic catalysts under identical conditions.
Alloyed catalysts will shift the product distribution toward more complete oxidation relative to unmodified catalysts.
The proposed mechanism applies under ambient-temperature, controlled-pH, controlled-ethanol-concentration conditions.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply under conditions that cause surface reconstruction or severe degradation.
Morphological changes may contribute to performance differences attributed to alloying.
